MOLECULAR GENETICS LABORATORY REPORT

Specimen Type: Peripheral blood
Collection Date: [redacted date]
Report Date: [redacted date]

REFERRAL REASON
Diagnostic evaluation for suspected Fragile-X syndrome

METHODOLOGY
PCR assay targeting FMR1 gene for FRAXA expansion mutations. This assay detects CGG repeat expansions in the FMR1 gene associated with Fragile-X syndrome. The test can reliably detect normal, premutation, and full mutation alleles.

FRAXA Allele Reference Ranges:
- Normal: <45 CGG repeats
- Intermediate: 45-54 CGG repeats
- Premutation: 55-200 CGG repeats
- Full mutation: >200 CGG repeats

RESULTS
FMR1 Gene Analysis:
Normal FRAXA alleles detected in FMR1 gene. No expansions in premutation or full mutation range.

Allele 1: 30 CGG repeats (Normal)
Allele 2: 29 CGG repeats (Normal)

INTERPRETATION
This pediatric patient shows two normal-sized FMR1 alleles, indicating absence of FRAXA expansion mutations. Based on these results, the patient is unlikely to have Fragile-X syndrome. It should be noted that this PCR-based assay specifically targets CGG repeat expansions and has a small possibility (<1%) of missing point mutations or structural rearrangements in the FMR1 gene that could potentially cause Fragile-X syndrome through alternative mechanisms.

Reported by: [redacted name], PhD
Laboratory Director: [redacted name], MD, PhD
